title.narrative: Percentage of HIV-positive results among the total HIV tests

description.narrative:
This indicator shows targets that are specific to the Litoral Province.
Baseline: Not available.
Targets: The national HIV strategic plan does not set targets for this indicator. Targets were set in consideration of known HIV positivity rates as found under ANC services, improved HIV testing and planned HIV case enrolment under TCS plus a 20% buffer during the three years of the grant while accounting for the implementation setup that will be needed in year 1 and then increasing case finding in years 2 and slightly downwards in Y3.
Measurement and Reporting: As reporting mechanisms for this indicator are not available, results for year 1 will be for data reported against the second half of the year only (October 2025-March 2026). Results in Y2 and Y3 were report on the full year and will come from the provincial level reporting system.

title.narrative: Proportion of population with access to an ITN within their household

description.narrative:
The baseline and targets are specific to the Continental Region and Annobon.
Baseline: 2011 DHS estimated that 20.5% of households had at least one LLIN for every two residents (i.e. access).
Targets: The target assumes 90% access achieved at time of distribution. The national strategic plan did not set targets for this indicator for the Continental region or Annobon.
Measurement and Reporting: Data for this indicator will come from the planned MIS study which will aligned to the mass distribution of LLIN planned for at the end of Y1 as the rainy season is between Feburary/March to October/November. The funds to implement the MIS are not covered under the grant and will come from the government. The reporting of this indicator will align to the reporting of coverage indicators of Y2 given the end dates of the rainy season and time for the report to be drafted and results validated.

title.narrative: Number of AIDS-related deaths per 100,000 population

description.narrative:
This indicator shows baseline and targets that are national.
Baseline: Corresponds to the national Spectrum estimated generated in 2022.
Targets: Set on the assumption that the rate of new infections will remain constant as a result of program efforts and aligned to national targets.
Measurement and reporting:The data source will be Spectrum. Dates of reporting results will be aligned with validation and release of results which is usually around May-June of the following year. Reported data will align to the calendar year which is not the same as the reporting cycle of this grant (April-March).

title.narrative: Proportion of children under five years old who slept under an insecticide-treated net the previous night

description.narrative:
The baseline and targets are specific to the Continental Region and Annobon.
Baseline: From the 2011 DHS survey, three years after the most recent LLIN distribution. In addition, the percentage of under-fives with at least one MILD and who slept under MILD the previous night was 53.5%.
Targets: The national strategic plan did not set targets for this indicator for the Continental Region or Annobon. The target assumes 70% post LLIN distribution.
Measurement and Reporting: Data for this indicator will come from the planned MIS study which will aligned to the mass distribution of LLIN planned for at the end of Y1 as the rainy season is between February/March to October/November. The funds to implement the MIS are not covered under the grant and will come from the government. The reporting of this indicator will align to the reporting of coverage indicators of Y2 given the end dates of the rainy season and time for the report to be drafted and results validated.

title.narrative: Confirmed malaria cases (microscopy or RDT): rate per 1000 persons per year

description.narrative:
The baseline and targets are specific to the Continental Region and Annobon.
Baseline: In 2022, there were 60,325 confirmed malaria cases in the Mainland and Annobon Island with an estimated population of 1132747 inhabitants in the mainland region and Annobon Island.
Targets: The national strategic plan did not set targets for this indicator for the continental region or Annobon. Targets were set assuming the largest decrease should occur between 2025 and 2026, following the planned LLIN distribution. The population estimates for 2025, 2026 and 2027 are: 255897, 1299853, and 1345348. This is on the 2015 Census applying a 3.5% ppoulation increase per year.
Measurement and Reporting: There is no digitilized reporting system on the mainland, but according to the Malaria NSP 2024-2028, it is foreseen to establish a robust data management system (DHIS2) and to strengthen the skills of HHAs for malaria data management in health facilities. On an annual basis, and alined to reporting for the coverage indicators, the national program will report the number of confirmed malaria cases against the established population estimates as found in this PF. Reported data will align to the calendar year which is not the same as the reporting cycle of this grant (April-March).

title.narrative: Percentage of people living with HIV who know their HIV status at the end of the reporting period

description.narrative:
This indicator shows baseline and targets that are national.
Baseline: 2022 Spectrum estimates.
Targets: Set in relation to historical data and in relation to planned activities (improved HIV testing in the general population and among pregnant women in the Litoral Province and natioanl efforts. Estimated number of PLHIV estimated from 2022 Spectrum estimate while adding a growth rate to both the adults (+15) and children (>15) populations as Spectrum projections were not available for 2025-2027 years at the time of this PF's development.
Measurement and reporting: The data source will be Spectrum. Dates of reporting results will be aligned with validation and release of results which is usually around May-June of the following year. Reported data will align to the calendar year which is not the same as the reporting cycle of this grant (April-March).
